findings.cross_file_justification: The floor fences (fence:FR-SZ*, fence:FR-1.2b) live in .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh and are only armed by the PreToolUse:Bash registration in .claude/settings.json; neither file is in floor_files and the hook row hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh is floor: false in guard-origins.yaml.
findings.description: floor.yaml claims the floor guards cannot be weakened by a cycle task, but the protection only pins the corpus rows and the floor: true row set. A change that removes the block-destructive-bash.sh registration from settings.json and drops its hook row from guard-origins.yaml passes guard-origins.bats (floor rows unchanged), floor-snapshot.bats (no floor file touched) and the corpus replay (which executes the script directly, not via the hook registration).
findings.failure_mode: All sixteen fence:* floor guards become inert in live sessions while every floor test stays green; the floor gives a false guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Either pin `.claude/settings.json` (or a dedicated registrations snapshot) in floor_files, or make guard-origins.bats assert that every floor fence's owning hook row exists and still carries the PreToolUse:Bash registration.

findings.cross_file_justification: The template comment states the text after `⇐` becomes the `--deps` flag when a bead is created; the kind token is now appended after that deps segment, so any deps extractor that reads to end of line (sprint-to-beads tooling, not in the visible diff) now receives `none · kind: mechanical`.
findings.description: The task-line grammar changed from `… ⇐ <blockers>` to `… ⇐ <blockers> · kind: <k>`. If the existing bead-creation parser slices from `⇐` to end of line, the deps string now contains the kind suffix and `none` is no longer recognised as the no-edge sentinel.
findings.failure_mode: Bead creation either fails to resolve `none · kind: mechanical` as a task reference or silently creates no dependency edges, breaking the executable DAG the comment promises.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the deps extractor strips a trailing ` · kind: …` segment (or stops at ` · `), and add a bats case with a template-shaped line; alternatively place the kind token before `⇐`.

findings.description: The else branch prints `30 d: no yield file (.run/guard-yield.json)` for every jq failure, including a yield file that exists but is malformed or missing `.totals`/`.window_days`. A corrupted or schema-drifted yield file is reported as absent.
findings.failure_mode: Operator reruns guard-yield.sh believing the file is missing; a schema mismatch between guard-yield.sh output and this reader is never surfaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish `[[ ! -f "$yf" ]]` (no yield file) from a jq parse/shape failure (`yield file unreadable`) in the fallback message.

findings.description: Adding a `paths:` frontmatter turns an always-loaded rule into a path-scoped one. Stash-safety governs `git stash` commands the model issues through the Bash tool in any session, not only edits to `*.sh`/`*.bats` files. In a session that touches no matching path the rule is not loaded at all.
findings.failure_mode: The model runs `git stash pop` style wraps without the rule in context; only the FR-1.2b fence (swallowed-output shapes) remains, so unswallowed but still index-shifting stash wraps are no longer discouraged.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep stash-safety unscoped (drop `paths:`) or add a short always-loaded pointer rule; keep the scoped frontmatter for skill-invariants.md where the scope is accurate.

findings.description: Replay tagging is driven by the ambient `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY` env var inherited by the hook process. If an operator or a shell profile exports it in a live session, every real block, override and marker row is tagged `replay: true`.
findings.failure_mode: guard-yield excludes genuine blocks from the 30-day yield, so the Guards line in loa-status under-reports real blocks and the register's yield data is silently wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Have run-corpus.sh pass the replay flag through a dedicated channel (e.g. a `.run/audit-replay` sentinel it creates and removes, or `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY_TOKEN` matched against a corpus-run id) and have guard-yield warn when replay rows appear outside a corpus run window.
